terms.comment: An established modern borrowing recorded by both modern references. The long ā follows Morgan–Owens’s marked forms.

evidence: Pliny, N.H. 12.24: arborī nōmen pālae, pōmō ariēnae
terms.comment: Traupman 70, alongside banāna; from Pliny’s Indian fruit. No modern fruit sense is presented as Classical.
Medieval, and Linnaeus’s genus name Musa.

terms.gloss: the Indian tree whose fruit is the ariena: the banana plant
terms.comment: Pliny’s name for the tree, beside ariēna for its fruit; Lewis & Short identifies it with the banana. The same form is pāla, a spade.

phrases.latin: Vidē: in hāc arbore banānae adhūc viridēs pendent.
phrases.english: Look: on this tree the bananas are still hanging green.

phrases.latin: Folium pālae tam lātum est ut nōs ab imbre tegat.
phrases.english: A banana leaf is so broad that it keeps the rain off us.

sources: Lewis & Short: pala
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: numbered food and kitchen sections
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 70–73.
